newsitem.title: EGYPT: Boutros-Ghali back in Egypt from United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali back in Egypt from United Nations.

text.p: Former U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali arrived home in Egypt on Saturday and said one aim of his unsuccessful campaign for a second term was to defend the independence of the U.N. secretariat.
Boutros-Ghali lost the job to Kofi Annan of Ghana after the United States vetoed a second term on the grounds that he had not done enough to reform the United Nations.

"The aim...was to defend the Egyptian presence at the United Nations and the objectives of the United Nations, which requires from the secretariat a minimum of independence," he told reporters at Cairo airport in the early hours.

Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who met him on arrival, said Boutros-Ghali's performance as secretary-general had been great and honourable. "He will give us his great experience in several fields," he added.
Boutros-Ghali will meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Saturday morning and will be the guest of honour at a reception by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri in the evening.
In Paris he said he would put himself at the disposal of Mubarak and Ganzouri and would not retire from politics.
